Session, II. 1815.

An Act Relative TO the Passing of Teams and Carriages in the Public Highways.

SECTION 1. BE it enacted by the General Assembly, by and BY the authority thereof, TO be enacted That it shall be the duty Of every person, driving or conducting any coach, chariot, chaise, sulky, wagon, cart, dray, or wheel carriage Of any kind or sled or sleigh, with any horse or horses, or with oxen, or any kind OF team, in any Of the highways, streets, lanes or gangways, in this State, when meeting another with carriage, sled, sleigh or team, of any Of the above mentioned description, when it shall be practicable, to conduct and keep such as shall be under his or her care, to the right hand side Of any such person, in any such highway, street, lane or gangway, so that the person met may pass on his or her left hand, and have as near as conveniently be the benefit OF one half Of the way; And that any such person, intentionally and wilfully failing to do so, shall forfeit and pay a fine, two dollars, TO be recovered with all lawful costs, by special action of the case, before any Justice Of the Peace Of the county where the offense shall be committed, for the use OF any person who shall sue for the same; and moreover shall be liable TO pay all special damages accruing from unnecessary delay or otherwise to any person or persons, by neglect or refusal to comply with the requisitions Of this act, to be covered by special action of the case by the said or persons so injured, in any court having cognizance thereof. Provided, however, that it shall be optional with the driver of any loaded team, when met or overtaken by an empty team, or any carriage above mentioned, either TO stop his team, until the team or carriage by which he shall be met or overtaken, shall have passed, if there be sufficient room, or TO give half the way aforesaid.

SECTION 2. And be IT further enacted, That any person having the charge of any such team as aforesaid, who shall negligently or wilfully leave the same TO go at large, in any such highway, street, lane or gangway, shall pay the same fine of Two dollars, TO be recovered and applied as aforesaid, IN an action to be brought against the owner, or the person having the care thereof aforesaid, at the election Of the plaintiff.

SECTION 3. And be it further enacted BY the Assembly, That this act shall take effect in six days from The rising of this Assembly, and be published in all the newspapers printed in the STATE.

SAMUEL EDDY, Secretary.
